title: The Global Representativeness Index: A Total Variation Distance Framework for Measuring Demographic Fidelity in Survey Research

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating the Global Representativeness Index (GRI) using Total Variation Distance to measure how closely a survey sample's country, region, and continent distributions match United Nations global population benchmarks.

Calculating the GRI using Total Variation Distance to measure the distributional fidelity between the sample's gender composition and UN global population benchmarks, often cross-tabulated with country and age.
Calculating the GRI using Total Variation Distance to compare the survey sample's age bracket distribution against UN global population benchmarks.
Calculating the GRI using Total Variation Distance to compare the survey sample's religious affiliation distribution against Pew Research Center global religious landscape benchmarks.
Calculating the GRI using Total Variation Distance to evaluate the representativeness of urban versus rural respondents compared to UN World Urbanization Prospects benchmarks.
